claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a disordered BCC phase near 1100°C.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a temperature-dependent reduction in the Gibbs-energy barrier for a disordered-to-ordered transformation.
Crossing a critical ordering-barrier value allows the thermodynamic propensity for ordering to overcome kinetic hindrance.
Crossing the critical barrier initiates local chemical ordering and subsequent phase transformation.
Machine-learning-assisted thermodynamic integration and DFT upsampling can calculate the full temperature dependence of vacancy migration Gibbs energies while including thermal excitations.
Temperature-dependent vacancy formation and migration Gibbs energies can be used to obtain ab initio self-diffusivities.
The cited computational framework is suitable for calculating vacancy-assisted diffusion activation energies in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 over 800–1100°C.
Temperature-dependent activation energies and local ordering free-energy profiles mediate the formation of short-range-ordered clusters in the BCC matrix.
Short-range ordering may involve Al–Cr enrichment.
At high temperature, configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC phase despite ordering tendencies.
Lowering temperature from 1100°C toward 800°C decreases the Gibbs-energy barrier for initiating local ordering.
Diffusion imposes the kinetic constraint that competes with the thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
A distinct temperature threshold will occur at which the ordering barrier drops dramatically.
The predicted barrier drop will correlate with lattice-parameter shifts and the emergence of ordering peaks in diffraction.
Lattice-parameter shifts and ordering peaks would identify the onset of transformation.
The proposed mechanism applies to equilibrium thermal treatments between 800°C and 1100°C.
Rapid quenching or additional alloying elements may change the proposed phase-stability behavior.
Anharmonicity can strongly affect temperature-dependent vacancy formation and migration Gibbs energies.
Machine-learning interatomic-potential approximations and the treatment of anharmonicity create quantitative uncertainty in the predicted barrier.
The exact critical ordering-barrier threshold may vary and requires experimental sensitivity analysis.
